# SELECTION: the first 500 characters

**502 characters in 62 themed units**: the 36 film characters of 《三十六个字》 plus **466 new signs**. The machine-readable list is [`selection.yaml`](selection.yaml), generated by [`tools/make_selection.py`](tools/make_selection.py) from its hand-curated unit plan. Every candidate with its data is in [`candidates.tsv`](candidates.tsv).

## Sources

| # | Source | Used for | How it was read |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **HSK 3.0**: 《国际中文教育中文水平等级标准》 (*Chinese Proficiency Grading Standards for International Chinese Language Education*, GF 0025-2021, Ministry of Education of the PRC / State Language Commission, 2021). Character list, Band I = levels 1–3 (300 characters each). | Early-literacy relevance (priority 1): level 1 first, then 2, then 3 | [Wiktionary: Appendix:HSK list of Mandarin words v3.0/characters](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Appendix:HSK_list_of_Mandarin_words_v3.0/characters), revision 89448185, parsed by `tools/candidates.py` |
| 2 | **CKIP word frequency** (Chinese Knowledge and Information Processing group, Academia Sinica): the 10,000 most frequent Mandarin words | Frequency tie-breaker. A character's rank = the best rank of any top-10,000 word that contains it (`ckip` in `selection.yaml`) | [Wiktionary: Appendix:Mandarin Frequency lists](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Appendix:Mandarin_Frequency_lists) (10 sub-pages, revisions 87160297–91542360) |
| 3 | **Wiktionary "Glyph origin"** sections (liushu labels: pictogram, ideogram, ideogrammic compound, phono-semantic compound, jiajie) | Visual explainability (priority 2) and the pedagogical order of the units | `tools/research.py` extracts (the same ones the writers use) |
| 4 | **Wikimedia Commons, Ancient Chinese characters project** (`File:<form>-oracle.svg`, `-bronze.svg`, `-seal.svg`, `-clerical-han.svg` / `-slip.svg` / `-silk.svg`) | Ancient forms available (priority 3): ≥2 stages preferred | `tools/fetch_glyphs_list.py --index-only` over the whole candidate pool |

> [!NOTE]
> The brief also suggests mainland **grade 1–2 literacy lists** (e.g. the 统编版《语文》一年级识字表). They are not available on Wikimedia, and network access was limited to Wikimedia, so they were **not** used. A human cross-check against them is listed as an open question in `REPORT.md`.

## Method

1. **Candidate pool (969)**: all 900 HSK 3.0 Band I characters (levels 1–3), plus 69 visually rich pictographs and compounds from higher levels that young children meet early (耳 牙 齿 舌 眉 爪 羽 虫 贝 鼠 兔 蛇 熊 川 泉 谷 丘 禾 瓜 豆 井 户 巾 皿 鼎 瓦 册 斗 尺 寸 矢 戈 刃 …). The 36 film characters were set aside (they already exist), leaving 946.
2. **Research and coverage for the whole pool**: Wiktionary extracts and a Commons index check for every candidate (`candidates.tsv` lists HSK level, CKIP rank, the first liushu label and the ancient stages found).
3. **Choice**, in the brief's priority order:
   - **HSK level 1 almost completely (284 of 300 incl. film characters).** Left out: 什 些 哪 净 (no Glyph origin on Wiktionary, so nothing accurate to say); 着 系 准 干 (one simplified form for several words, abstract, few or no ancient forms); 场 商 院 绍 馆 差 试 票 (adult or travel vocabulary with an unclear origin or 0–1 ancient stages).
   - **HSK level 2: 116 of 300**, chosen for children's everyday words (family, food, body, animals, colours, weather) and for pictographs/compounds with ancient forms. Abstract level-2 words with no ancient forms (但 所 经 该 应 际 …) were left for later.
   - **HSK level 3 and above, or not in HSK: 82**, almost all pictographs or compounds with 2–4 ancient stages (足 首 皮 龙 立 父 土 止 齿 耳 牙 舌 眉 爪 羽 鼠 兔 …), plus a few phono-semantic animal words (蛇 熊 猪 鸭 鹅 狼).
   - Where two candidates were equally relevant, the one with more ancient stages won.
4. **Units of 6–10**, themed, in the brief's pedagogical order: pictographs (units 1–20), ideograms (21–24), compound ideograms (25–39), phono-semantic characters grouped by their meaning part (40–62: 口 mouth, 讠 speech, 氵 water, 扌 hand, 亻 person, 心 heart, 辶 walking, 犭 animal, 纟 silk, 钅 metal, 木 wood …). The 36 film characters sit in the units where they fit (nature, plants, animals, tools, home); 叟 (a hand holding a torch) joins "Fire, Light and Shadow".

| | Selected (incl. film) | HSK Band I list |
|---|---|---|
| HSK level 1 | 284 | 300 |
| HSK level 2 | 116 | 300 |
| HSK level 3 | 37 | 300 |
| HSK levels 4–9 (Bands II–III) | 49 | — |
| other (13 film characters outside Band I; 皿 臼 刃, not in HSK 3.0) | 16 | — |

**New signs by ancient stages found on Commons:** 4 stages 132 · 3 stages 114 · 2 stages 55 · 1 stage 74 · none 91 (these get `journey: []`; most are frequent phono-semantic words such as 你 他 们 吃 妈 爸 that have no files in the ACC project). Final numbers are in `REPORT.md` and `glyph-coverage.json`.

## Composite ids (one simplified form, several traditional characters)

| id | sense kids need | the other character(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `后-後` | after, behind (以后, 后面) | 后 queen |
| `里-裡` | inside (里面, 家里) | 里 village / *li* (distance) |
| `几-幾` | how many (几个) | 几 small table |
| `发-發` | to send out, to start (出发, 发现); its ancient form is a bow shooting an arrow | 髮 hair (头发) |
| `只-隻` | measure word for animals and birds (一只猫); a hand holding one bird | 只 only |
| `钟-鐘` | bell, clock (钟表) | 鍾 cup / surname |

Same-form senses (no composite id needed): 面 face/side (not 麵 noodles), 谷 valley (not 穀 grain), 斗 dipper/ladle, *dǒu* (not 鬥 fight), 了 (not 瞭), 别 別 (not 彆), 才 (not 纔), 向 (not 嚮), 杯 (not 盃). 干 乾/幹/干, 台 臺/檯/颱, 松 鬆/松, 冲 衝/沖, 系 係/繫, 着 著 and 准 準 were left out for now (see `REPORT.md`).

## Journey overrides

`journey: default` looks up oracle, bronze, seal and clerical forms on the **traditional** character. Five signs need an explicit list because Commons files their early forms under another character (checked with `--index-only`):

| id | journey | why |
|---|---|---|
| 气 | 气 (oracle, bronze) → 氣 (seal, clerical) | 气 is the original vapour pictograph; 米 was added later (氣); simplified 气 went back to the old form, like the film's 云/雲 |
| 从 | 从 (oracle) → 從 (bronze, seal) | 从, two people walking one behind the other, is the original; 辵 was added later (從) |
| 虫 | 虫 (oracle, bronze, seal) | 虫 (a snake) is the original pictograph; 蟲 (three 虫) has no files |
| 两 | 两 (bronze, seal) | Commons files the ancient forms of 兩 under 两 |
| 内 | 内 (oracle, bronze, seal, clerical) | Commons files the ancient forms of 內 under 内 |

Other simplified forms that have files of their own (几, 里, 只, 个, 写, 体, 医) were **not** used, because there they are different words (几 table, 里 village, 只 only, 体 *bèn*, 医 quiver …).

The unit grouping uses the first liushu label on Wiktionary; a few units mix types on purpose (numbers, colours, directions). Each sign's final `origin.type` is decided from its research extract when it is written, so it can differ from the unit's heading (for example 我 is grouped with the pictographs but typed `loan`, because "I" is a sound-borrowing).
